title: The Lehrhaus Runs Backwards
hook: Rosenzweig's house of learning began from adults' lives and moved toward the text
carry: learning runs from your life back to the torah
tomorrow: why keep teaching when your students can't leave the camp?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rosenzweig and the leather straps he hadn't taken up yet. Not yet: a door you're facing, not one you've closed. Today, the same man opens a school, and runs it backwards.

The essay prompt on Noa's screen says: describe a tradition that has shaped you. She stares at it. She knows the Shabbat songs, a few stories, her grandfather's soup ladle. She doesn't feel like she knows enough Torah to write a word. Rosenzweig would have said she's starting in exactly the right place. In Frankfurt he opened a house of learning for adults, the Lehrhaus. And he said its learning had to run in reverse order.
screen: `DESCRIBE A TRADITION THAT SHAPED YOU.` → `I DON'T KNOW ENOUGH.` → `LEARNING IN REVERSE.`

segments.voice: In his opening address, Rosenzweig described the old way. A child grew up inside the text, and learning flowed out from the Torah into life. But the adults walking into his Lehrhaus had grown up far from that. Their lives were full of other things: work, science, art, cities. So he turned the direction around. Start from the edge, from life as you're living it, and travel back toward the center, the text. Nobody had to pretend to be closer than they were. The questions people brought from home and work were the doorway. The Torah has a line that sounds like his permission slip: "But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it." Near, not across an ocean. So for Noa the answer isn't to memorize something impressive by Friday. Start with the ladle, the packing, the move. Ask what it's about. Then go looking for the text that has already asked it. That's the thing to repeat tonight: Rosenzweig didn't lower the bar. He moved the starting line to where people actually stand.
screen: `THE OLD WAY: TEXT INTO LIFE.` · `NOW: START FROM YOUR LIFE.` · `THE WORD IS VERY NIGH.` · `MOVE THE STARTING LINE.` · then, large: `FROM LIFE TO TEXT.`

segments.voice: Name one question your week has handed you, about a move, a choice, a person. Then make a small plan: what you want to understand, what usually stops you from looking, and one place you'll look first, a verse, a book or someone older than you.
screen: `ONE QUESTION FROM THIS WEEK.` · `WHAT STOPS YOU?` · `ONE PLACE TO LOOK.`
